items.title: The module of maps into a torsion free module is torsion free
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that Hom_R(M, N) is torsion free whenever N is, for arbitrary modules over a domain, and the author's proof is a two-line containment argument (statement lines 4995-4998, proof lines 5001-5004). It chooses a surjection from a direct sum of copies of R onto M and uses it to realise Hom_R(M, N) as a submodule of a product of copies of N (proof lines 5002-5003). The non-formal content is the choice of presentation and the direction of the induced map: the surjection on the first variable of Hom gives an injection into the product with Man itself, whereas the opposite arrow would be the wrong way. The reader also has to notice that the assertion is about torsion elements, which are tested elementwise, so a submodule of a product of torsion free modules is again torsion free.
